problem: Speech-guided robot grounding pipelines cascade ASR into text-based language grounding, so ASR misconversions caused by speaker variability and noise (e.g., Korean 'bicycle' heard as 'white one') directly break target-object grounding.
motivation: Spoken language is an accessible interface for non-expert and disabled users of assistive robots, but grounding depends entirely on transcription accuracy. The authors observe that acoustically similar words have nearby ASR latent encodings, so passing the latent speech vector to the grounding network can recover the intended word despite misrecognition.
key_idea: Feed the ASR encoder's latent speech vector, together with the transcribed text and a GAT-encoded scene graph, into a DistilKoBERT grounding network trained end-to-end, so acoustic similarity compensates for misrecognized words.
insight: The ablation shows the latent speech vector matters: removing v_speech drops accuracy from 85.3% to 77.0%, and SGGNet² even beats a text-only variant given ground-truth transcripts (80.7%), so the latent carries information beyond clean text. The PCA visualization shows similar-sounding words lie close in the latent space regardless of meaning. Also, original SGGNet with ASR text collapses to 26.7%, showing how fragile cascaded pipelines are.
method: Korean ASR: NeMo Conformer-CTC pre-trained on KsponSpeech (620k utterances, 965 h, SpecAugment, 20 epochs), then trained jointly with grounding
Scene-graph generator: YOLO detection + adaptive LiDAR point-cloud clustering give 3-D positions; a rule-based conversion produces a graph with left/right/front/behind edge predicates
Scene-graph encoder: DistilKoBERT encodes node classes and edge predicates (128-d), a GAT updates nodes, and max-pool readout gives v_sg (128-d)
Speech latent vectors: the ASR encoder's hidden states (256-d, T=126) are projected by a linear layer to 756-d as v_speech'
Grounding transformer: DistilKoBERT takes [CLS], v_sg', v_speech', ASR text tokens, [SEP]; a linear head on [CLS] classifies the target object (cross-entropy, AdamW, ~200 epochs)
Navigation system: FAST-LIO2 metric SLAM, move_base planning and semantic SLAM on a Jetson Orin, sending the grounded target to a quadruped

setting.backbone: NeMo Conformer-CTC ASR + GAT + DistilKoBERT (trained end-to-end after ASR pre-training)
setting.training_data: KsponSpeech (620k utterances, 965 h) for ASR pre-training; synthetic Korean navigation dataset of 13,650 commands (9,750 train / 3,900 test), 10 target classes, 35 object names, TTS speech (Naver Clova, 10 voices) with random scene graphs
setting.observation: Speech audio (5 s, 24 kHz) + RGB image (YOLO) + LiDAR point cloud -> scene graph
setting.action_space: Selects a target object; navigation is then via move_base speed/direction commands on the quadruped
setting.simulator: real world only (no simulator; grounding evaluated on a synthetic dataset)
setting.privileged: none at test time in the demo, but the map and scene graph were built in advance with 5 objects placed (pre-exploration)

numbers.extra: synthetic TTS speech, non-overlapping object names between train and test
numbers.evidence: Table 1: SGGNet² (Ours), input Λ, grounding accuracy 85.3

numbers_note: Only a custom grounding-accuracy benchmark; no standard navigation benchmark, and the real-robot demo is qualitative with no success rates.
results: SGGNet² reaches 85.3% grounding accuracy, about 8 points above the variant without the latent speech vector (77.0%) and about 5 points above the Modified SGGNet with ground-truth text (80.7%). The original SGGNet with ASR text gets only 26.7%. A qualitative real-robot demo on an RBQ-3 quadruped grounds the target among five candidates, including under pillar occlusion.
limitations: Evaluated only on a small synthetic dataset (templated commands, TTS voices, 10 classes) with no real human speech or noise evaluation
Real-robot demo is qualitative and small-scale (5 objects, pre-built map, no success-rate statistics)
Korean-only, with commands limited to a verb + preposition + object pattern
